questions.q: Which drill uses a rotating roller bit at the end of a drill stem to grind or crush rock?
questions.ref: Peurifoy, Schexnayder & Shapira, Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods - excavation, drilling and construction equipment
questions.n: Rotary blasthole drills commonly use roller-cone or similar bits to crush rock as the drill string rotates.

questions.q: What are flying forms?
o: Large prefabricated table-form units moved from bay to bay or floor to floor
questions.ref: ACI 347R - Guide to Formwork for Concrete
questions.n: Flying or table forms are large reusable floor-form assemblies moved as units between placements.

questions.q: Which professional discipline typically directs soil and foundation investigations for a building project?
questions.ref: FHWA Geotechnical Engineering Circulars - subsurface investigation, boring and soil-testing guidance
questions.n: Geotechnical engineers investigate soil, rock, groundwater, and foundation behavior.

questions.q: Which machine combines a front loader with a rear excavating backhoe?
questions.ref: Caterpillar Performance Handbook - earthmoving and grading equipment functions
questions.n: A backhoe-loader combines a loader bucket at the front with a backhoe excavator attachment at the rear.

questions.q: What construction method uses forms that move continuously or in small increments upward as concrete placement progresses?
questions.ref: ACI 347R - Guide to Formwork for Concrete
questions.n: Slipforms move vertically as concrete is continuously placed, commonly for cores, silos, and tall walls.

questions.q: Using a jackhammer is an example of which basic drilling action?
questions.ref: Peurifoy, Schexnayder & Shapira, Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods - excavation, drilling and construction equipment
questions.n: A jackhammer breaks material through rapid repeated impacts, which is percussion action.

questions.q: What is proof rolling used to evaluate?
o: The uniformity and support condition of prepared subgrade or base
questions.ref: FHWA Geotechnical Engineering Circulars - subsurface investigation, boring and soil-testing guidance
questions.n: Proof rolling uses loaded equipment to reveal weak or unstable areas in prepared soil-support systems.

questions.q: What is earthmoving?
o: The excavation, transport, placement, and shaping of soil or rock
questions.ref: Peurifoy, Schexnayder & Shapira, Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods - excavation, drilling and construction equipment
questions.n: Earthmoving broadly includes excavating, loading, hauling, placing, and grading earth materials.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of reusable large-panel or table-form systems on repetitive projects?
o: Faster cycling with reduced repetitive assembly labor
They remove all structural design requirements
questions.ref: ACI 347R - Guide to Formwork for Concrete
questions.n: Large reusable forms reduce repeated setup and dismantling effort where floor plans repeat.

questions.q: Why is proof rolling useful before placing a slab or pavement?
o: It helps identify localized weak zones that may deform under load
questions.ref: FHWA Geotechnical Engineering Circulars - subsurface investigation, boring and soil-testing guidance
questions.n: Visible deflection or rutting during proof rolling can indicate inadequate support or poorly compacted areas.

questions.q: Which type of drill is designed to recover a cylindrical rock sample for examination?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - earthwork, equipment, formwork and drilling terminology
questions.n: Core drilling cuts an annular kerf and retrieves a cylindrical rock or concrete core.

questions.q: A project needs one machine to excavate utility trenches, load spoil, and perform light backfilling. Which equipment is the most versatile choice?
questions.ref: Caterpillar Performance Handbook - earthmoving and grading equipment functions
questions.n: A backhoe-loader combines digging and loading functions in one machine.

questions.q: A high-rise residential project repeats nearly identical room-sized cells, and the contractor wants to cast walls and slabs in one operation. Which system fits best?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - sitework, excavation, foundations, concrete formwork and construction equipment
questions.n: Tunnel forms are intended for repetitive cellular layouts where walls and slabs are concreted together.

questions.q: Which field test records the number of hammer blows needed to drive a split-barrel sampler into soil?
questions.ref: ASTM D1586/D1586M - Standard Test Method for Standard Penetration Test (SPT) and Split-Barrel Sampling of Soils
questions.n: The SPT records penetration resistance as a blow count during split-barrel sampling.

questions.q: Which reusable forming system casts walls and slabs together in repetitive cellular construction?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - sitework, excavation, foundations, concrete formwork and construction equipment
questions.n: Tunnel forms create room-sized wall-and-slab cells and are well suited to repetitive apartments, hotels, and similar buildings.

questions.q: When shallow near-surface conditions must be examined directly, which investigation method is most appropriate?
questions.ref: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Geotechnical Investigations / subsurface exploration guidance
questions.n: A test pit exposes soil directly and is useful for shallow subsurface inspection where excavation is practical.

questions.q: What does SPT stand for?
questions.ref: ASTM D1586/D1586M - Standard Test Method for Standard Penetration Test (SPT) and Split-Barrel Sampling of Soils
questions.n: ASTM D1586 defines the Standard Penetration Test using a split-barrel sampler driven into soil.

questions.q: What is a test boring?
o: A drilled subsurface exploration used to obtain soil/rock information and samples
questions.ref: FHWA Geotechnical Engineering Circulars - subsurface investigation, boring and soil-testing guidance
questions.n: Test borings provide direct subsurface information and permit sampling, groundwater observations, and in-situ tests.

questions.q: A concrete core must rise continuously as placement proceeds, with the forms moving upward rather than being dismantled each lift. What method is appropriate?
questions.ref: ACI 347R - Guide to Formwork for Concrete
questions.n: Continuous upward movement of the form during placement identifies slipforming.

questions.q: What term describes soil or material placed to raise an area to the required elevation?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - earthwork, equipment, formwork and drilling terminology
questions.n: Fill is material placed and compacted to raise or reshape ground elevations.

questions.q: What is a climbing crane?
o: A crane designed to raise its mast or support as the building rises
A stationary derrick that cannot rise
A crane used only below grade
questions.ref: OSHA construction guidance - cranes, derricks, excavation and lifting terminology
questions.n: Climbing cranes are arranged so the crane can climb with the advancing building structure.

questions.q: What is cut and fill?
o: Excavating material from high areas and placing it in low areas to achieve design grades
Sawing lumber and filling nail holes
Cutting reinforcing bars and filling joints
questions.ref: Peurifoy, Schexnayder & Shapira, Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods - excavation, drilling and construction equipment
questions.n: Cut-and-fill operations redistribute earth to create the intended site profile.

questions.q: Which machine is primarily intended for fine grading and finishing long surfaces?
questions.ref: Caterpillar Performance Handbook - earthmoving and grading equipment functions
questions.n: Motor graders use a long adjustable blade for fine grading and surface finishing.

questions.q: Which drilling method breaks rock primarily through repeated impact blows?
questions.ref: Peurifoy, Schexnayder & Shapira, Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods - excavation, drilling and construction equipment
questions.n: Percussion drilling fragments rock through repeated impact energy.

questions.q: Which machine is especially useful when both excavation and loading/finishing tasks must be handled by one compact unit?
questions.ref: Caterpillar Performance Handbook - earthmoving and grading equipment functions
questions.n: The backhoe-loader's front bucket and rear excavator make it versatile for excavation, loading, backfilling, and light finishing tasks.

questions.q: What is hauling in site construction?
o: Transporting excavated or construction material from one location to another
questions.ref: Peurifoy, Schexnayder & Shapira, Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods - excavation, drilling and construction equipment
questions.n: Hauling refers to transporting excavated soil, aggregate, debris, or other material within or away from the site.

questions.q: What is a derrick?
o: A hoisting device using a mast or boom with ropes or cables
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - earthwork, equipment, formwork and drilling terminology
questions.n: A derrick is a hoisting device with a boom or mast used to raise and move loads by cables.

questions.q: What does grading mean in site construction?
o: Shaping the ground to required elevations and slopes
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - sitework, excavation, foundations, concrete formwork and construction equipment
questions.n: Grading cuts, fills, and shapes the ground surface to the required design elevations and drainage slopes.
